# Computing Environment

HPM 883 uses a three-tier computing environment designed to minimize setup friction while teaching reproducible research workflows.

::: callout-tip
## Quick Links

-   [Student Setup Guide](Resources/setup-guide.qmd) — Complete installation instructions
-   [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) — Common problems and solutions
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Two-Tier Architecture

| Tier | Platform | When to Use | Cost |
|-----------------|-----------------|----------------------|-----------------|
| **Primary** | [GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces) | Labs, code-alongs, assignments | Free (180 core-hours/month) |
| **Alternative** | Local (Positron/RStudio) + GitHub | Advanced users, offline work | Free |

### Tier 1: GitHub Codespaces (Primary)

For in-class exercises and all labs, we use **GitHub Codespaces** — a browser-based development environment that runs a full RStudio Server in your browser with zero local setup.

**Benefits:**

-   Zero installation — works on any computer with a browser
-   Pre-configured with all required R packages
-   Professional workflow (Git/GitHub integrated)
-   Free for verified students (180 core-hours/month)

**How it works:**

1.  Accept an assignment via GitHub Classroom link
2.  Click "Open in Codespace" → browser-based RStudio launches
3.  Work on your assignment
4.  Commit and push when done — no download/upload needed

**GitHub Organization Link:** <https://github.com/HPM-883-2026>

### Tier 2: Local Development (Alternative)

For the capstone project or if you prefer working offline, you can work locally using VS Code, **Positron** (recommended) or RStudio.

**Why local development?**

-   Works offline
-   Built-in AI assistance (Positron)
-   More computing power for large datasets
-   Full control over environment

**Setup required:** See [Local Setup for Labs](#local-setup) below.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Required Software

### R (version 4.3+)

R is our primary analysis language.

**Windows:**

``` bash
winget install --id R-project.R
```

**macOS:**

``` bash
brew install --cask r
```

### Positron (Recommended IDE)

[Positron](https://positron.posit.co/) is Posit's new IDE with built-in AI assistance.

| Feature               | Positron | RStudio          |
|-----------------------|----------|------------------|
| Built-in AI assistant | ✓        | ✗                |
| Active development    | ✓        | Maintenance only |
| VS Code extensions    | ✓        | Limited          |
| Price                 | Free     | Free             |

**Download:** [positron.posit.co](https://positron.posit.co/)

**Alternative:** [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) if you prefer.

### Git

Version control for all assignments.

**Windows:**

``` bash
winget install Git.Git
```

**macOS:**

``` bash
brew install git
```

**Configure:**

``` bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "your.email@unc.edu"
```

### Quarto

Publishing system for labs and reports. Usually bundled with Positron/RStudio.

**Verify installation:**

``` bash
quarto --version
```

**If not installed:** [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/)

## Workflow by Assignment Type

### In-Class Labs 

**Platform:** GitHub Codespaces

1.  Accept the code-along assignment via GitHub Classroom link
2.  Click "Open in Codespace" — RStudio opens in your browser
3.  Follow along with instructor
4.  Push your work when done (or discard if not needed)

### Problem Sets

**Platform:** GitHub Codespaces

1.  Accept assignment via GitHub Classroom link (distributed via Canvas)
2.  Click "Open in Codespace" — RStudio opens in your browser
3.  Complete the lab in `analysis.qmd`
4.  Render to HTML: `quarto render`
5.  Commit and push from the RStudio Git pane (or terminal):

``` bash
git add .
git commit -m "Complete Lab X"
git push
```

### Capstone Project

**Platform:** GitHub Codespaces or Local

For the capstone project, you may use either Codespaces or local development. The capstone template includes:

-   `analysis/01-pap.qmd` — Pre-analysis plan
-   `analysis/02-analysis.qmd` — Main analysis
-   `analysis/03-results.qmd` — Results summary
-   `_targets.R` — Analysis pipeline (optional)

## Reproducibility with renv

All course projects use [renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) for package management.

**First time opening a project:**

``` r
renv::restore()
```

This installs the exact package versions used to create the project.

**If you add new packages:**

``` r
install.packages("new_package")
renv::snapshot()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Local Setup for Labs {#local-setup}

If you prefer working locally instead of Codespaces, follow these steps for each lab assignment.

### Step 1: Clone the Assignment Repo

After accepting the GitHub Classroom assignment, clone your personal copy:

``` bash
git clone https://github.com/HPM-883-2026/lab-2-YOUR-USERNAME.git
cd lab-2-YOUR-USERNAME
```

Replace `YOUR-USERNAME` with your GitHub username. You can find the exact URL on the GitHub Classroom assignment page (green "Code" button → HTTPS).

### Step 2: Open in Your IDE

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Positron (Recommended)

1. Open Positron
2. **File → Open Folder** → select the cloned repo folder
3. Positron auto-detects R projects and activates `renv`

#### RStudio

1. Open RStudio
2. **File → Open Project** → select the `.Rproj` file in the repo folder
3. RStudio auto-detects `renv` and prompts for package restore

#### VS Code

1. Open VS Code
2. **File → Open Folder** → select the cloned repo folder
3. Install the [R Extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=REditorSupport.r) and [Quarto Extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=quarto.quarto) if not already installed
4. Open the R terminal (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P → "R: Create R Terminal")
:::

### Step 3: Restore Packages

Each lab uses `renv` to lock package versions. Run this **once** per project:

``` r
renv::restore()
```

This installs the exact same packages and versions used in Codespaces. It may take a few minutes the first time.

### Step 4: Run Code Chunks

Open the `.qmd` file and run chunks interactively:

- **Positron / VS Code:** Click the green play button on each chunk, or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter
- **RStudio:** Click "Run Current Chunk" (green arrow), or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter

### Step 5: Commit and Push

When you're done, save your work and push to GitHub:

``` bash
git add .
git commit -m "Complete Lab 2"
git push
```

Or use the Git pane in RStudio/Positron (Stage → Commit → Push).

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

### Package Installation Fails

``` r
# Delete cached packages and retry
unlink("renv/library", recursive = TRUE)
renv::restore()
```

### Git Push Rejected

``` bash
# Pull remote changes first
git pull --rebase
git push
```

### Quarto Render Fails

1.  Check YAML header for syntax errors
2.  Look for unmatched brackets or quotes
3.  Run chunks one-by-one to find the error

### Codespaces Running Slow

1.  Stop unused Codespaces: [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces) → Stop/Delete
2.  Use a larger machine type: ... menu → Change machine type → 4-core
3.  Clear old outputs: delete `_freeze/` folder

### Codespaces Won't Start

1.  Check your monthly quota: [github.com/settings/billing](https://github.com/settings/billing)
2.  Delete unused Codespaces to free quota
3.  Verify GitHub Education status: [education.github.com/pack](https://education.github.com/pack)

### GitHub Authentication Issues

``` bash
# Regenerate SSH key
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your.email@unc.edu"
# Add to GitHub: Settings → SSH Keys → New
```
